expected_level_description: You can: - determine the approach for your role within the team's delivery methodology - define and agree the scope of delivery for your role within a multidisciplinary team - negotiate and agree delivery priorities with the team and relevant stakeholders - clearly communicate the value of iterative delivery and realising benefits early

You can: - advise others how to ensure appropriate test coverage, data and scenarios, in line with acceptance criteria - analyse business risk and impacts of defects so that appropriate action can be taken to enable business acceptance - provide assurance on the suitability, business readiness and viability of delivered solutions

You can: - guide the selection and use of business modelling techniques to ensure consistency - define and share good practices for eliciting appropriate information to create effective models - create models and diagrams that represent complex and large-scale situations, aligning with and informing architecture artefacts - use business modelling outcomes to support strategic decision making

You can: - lead process analysis and evaluation to define business performance problems and opportunities - lead analysis and evaluation to design, test, implement and assess business process improvements - manage the design, execution and assessment of business process tests and usability evaluations

You can: - lead benefits and impact analysis for initiatives, including identifying trade-offs, quantitative and qualitative benefits, and business readiness indicators - ensure change impacts and benefits are translated into clear operating actions, ownership and measures - work across the business and with other professions to define and guide adoption and business readiness activities

You can: - lead the approach to understanding the context, the problem and root causes - set goals for a piece of work that aligns to the organisation's strategic context - lead the approach to developing and evaluating multiple options, sharing and advocating for recommendations to gain support

skill: Defining and managing business needs, user needs and requirements
expected_level_description: You can: - lead the elicitation, analysis and validation of complex or large-scale business and user needs, negotiating and addressing conflicts - define and assure artefacts, such as problem statements, epics, features, user stories, acceptance criteria and non-functional requirements, to communicate business and user needs - lead and define the approach to manage artefacts and ensure traceability - facilitate the prioritisation of needs, aligning to strategic goals

You can: - lead the analysis of functionality that systems deliver or need to deliver - create, and support others in the creation of, system and data models and documentation - assess the effect of system changes and share them with relevant stakeholders - determine when and how you and your team work with others to identify gaps in functionality and user experience, and their impact

You can: - work with the team to develop and maintain an understanding of stakeholders - work with the team to develop and implement stakeholder communications strategies - identify and resolve issues, influence stakeholders and manage relationships effectively - build long-term strategic relationships and communicate clearly and regularly with stakeholders

You can: - synthesise insights from multiple appropriate sources of evidence to provide a holistic understanding of user experience - identify patterns, root causes, and opportunities for improvement across journeys - ensure user experience insights are clearly linked to requirements, priorities, and design decisions - identify priorities for improving user experience, taking into consideration business and technical constraints

You can: - analyse how a service fits into care pathways across organisations - work with clinicians, care staff, and patients to shape digital services - explain the effect of digital decisions on care, safety, and staff workload
You can: - take part in hazard workshops and contribute to a hazard log - follow the clinical risk management process for your work - provide evidence for a clinical safety case, such as test results
You can: - apply data protection principles to your work - contribute to data protection impact assessments - handle information requests and records correctly
You can: - read and use FHIR resources, profiles, and APIs - build or test simple integrations under guidance - check messages against a specification
You can: - find and use the right codes for a data item or form - use terminology browsers and reference sets
You can: - supervise day-to-day work and give feedback - take part in recruitment and induction - hold regular one-to-one conversations
